one_liner: BSD-2 C++ HTJ2K (JPEG 2000 Part 15) codec; its lossless decode ran 6-16x faster than OpenJPEG's Part 1 decode.
what_it_does: OpenJPH encodes and decodes High-Throughput JPEG 2000 (ISO/IEC 15444-15, ITU-T T.814) codestreams, reusing the Part 1 wavelets (reversible 5/3, irreversible 9/7) but only the HT block coder. The API is ojph::codestream: set SIZ/COD/QCD parameters, then push image rows with exchange() when encoding or pull them with pull() when decoding, one line and one component at a time. It is not an OpenJPEG drop-in. It cannot decode ordinary Part 1 (EBCOT) files, and its tools write raw .j2c codestreams without the .jph box header.
how_it_is_fast: The HT block coder replaces JPEG 2000's bit-plane-by-bit-plane MQ arithmetic coding (EBCOT) with a single cleanup pass. That pass codes 2x2 quads through three byte streams: an adaptive run-length MEL coder, table-driven VLC codewords (table0.h/table1.h) and raw MagSgn bits, plus optional SigProp/MagRef refinement passes. Decoding is mostly table lookups and bit extraction instead of one context-modelled binary decision per bit. The wavelet and colour transforms work line by line, which keeps memory small, and on x86-64 the block coder and transforms dispatch at runtime to SSE/SSSE3/AVX2/AVX-512 kernels. There are also VSX (POWER8/9) and WebAssembly SIMD paths.
when_to_use: Lossless storage of medical images under the DICOM HTJ2K transfer syntaxes (1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.201/202/203), where you control the encoder and decode latency matters (1.4-1.5 ms per 512x512 12/16-bit slice on an M1 Pro in the measured run).
You need an open-source (BSD-2-Clause) HTJ2K encoder as well as a decoder, and Kakadu's licence is not an option.
Streaming or low-memory pipelines that can feed or consume one image row at a time through exchange()/pull().
Decoding in browsers or Node.js through the provided WebAssembly SIMD build.
OpenEXR HTJ2K compression, which builds on OpenJPH (it appears as HTJ2K_32/HTJ2K_256 in the catalogued meshoptimizer harness, and issue #273 comes from an OpenEXR 3.4.11 user).
when_not_to_use: Existing JPEG 2000 Part 1 archives or third-party .jp2/.j2k files: OpenJPH implements only the HT block coder. Use OpenJPEG or Grok, or transcode first.
Raw speed above all: in the same dicom-codecs run, Kakadu's HTJ2K decode was 2.4x to 3.6x faster (derived) than OpenJPH (for example 29.36 vs 89.20 ms on the 3064x4664 mammogram).

Multi-core decoding of one large image: OpenJPH has no internal threading (no thread options in the API or in ojph_compress/ojph_expand), while OpenJPEG, Grok and Kakadu can parallelise across code blocks. The benchmark ran every codec single-threaded and compiled OpenJPEG's threading out.

ARM targets that need SIMD: the CMake ARM section is empty and src/core/coding has no NEON kernels, so aarch64 (including Apple Silicon) runs the generic C++ path. Open issue #273 also reports a SIGSEGV in the scalar encoder's mem_elastic_allocator on arm64.
Rate-controlled lossy encoding to a byte or bitrate target: docs/status.md says only quantisation-step lossy is implemented, with no rate control.

integration.form: static or shared lib (CMake; BUILD_SHARED_LIBS defaults to ON)
integration.dependencies: none for the library; libtiff for TIFF I/O in the command-line tools (OJPH_ENABLE_TIFF_SUPPORT defaults to ON, can be turned off); emscripten for the wasm build
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.12; C++14 by default (the CMake comment says C++11 suffices for the library, C++14 is for gtest); C11 for aligned_alloc
integration.platforms: x86-64 (runtime dispatch over SSE through AVX-512), ppc64le (VSX kernels, POWER8+), WebAssembly SIMD, aarch64 and other targets generic C++ only; little- and big-endian handled
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the library does no internal threading, so the usual pattern is one ojph::codestream object per thread

gotchas: Decoded line_buf samples are not clamped to the component bit depth; callers must clamp them, as the dicom-codecs wrapper does (OpenJPH issue #35). For colour without a colour transform, set_planar(true) takes a faster path (issue #34).
Release 0.31.0 broke API and ABI compatibility, so pin a version. Issues #303 and #304 report a broken openjph-config-version.cmake in 0.30.0 and unusual shared-library names.

Strict-aliasing type punning in the block decoders made GCC 15/16 (MinGW, -O2/-O3) produce silently wrong multipass irreversible decodes (issue #279, fixed in 0.30.0). Avoid older releases with recent GCC. The open crash issues are #273 (arm64 scalar encoder) and #374 (segfault with very small qstep values).
'.raw' files are read as little-endian, unlike Kakadu and OpenJPEG ('.rawl'), and docs/usage_examples.md says this convention is planned to change.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over CharLS when you want a wavelet codec with resolution scalability and faster lossless decode: CharLS decoded 1.8-2.4x slower in the same run, although CharLS reads standard JPEG-LS data that OpenJPH cannot. Pick Grok or OpenJPEG instead when you must read Part 1 JPEG 2000 files or want multi-threaded decoding of large images.
verified_claims_summary: dicom-codecs (a third-party, WIP DICOM wrapper; tests/main.cpp and tests/benchmark.cpp) was run on an Apple M1 Pro with an unnamed compiler: each codec encoded four raw images losslessly with its own encoder, then one warm-up and one timed decode. OpenJPH took 4.09/1.43/1.53/89.20 ms against OpenJPEG's 24.73/15.65/22.27/1447.63 ms (about 6x-16x, derived). OpenJPEG was decoding a Part 1 EBCOT stream while OpenJPH decoded its own HTJ2K stream, so the ratio measures format plus library together. OpenJPH ran its generic non-SIMD path on arm64, OpenJPEG was built single-threaded with -ffast-math, and OpenJPEG's own HTJ2K decoder was not timed.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-01, release 0.32.0, 296 stars, 91 forks, 31 open issues, packaged in several distributions per repology) under BSD-2-Clause. It is copyable, but the measured numbers come from a December 2023 snapshot (pinned commit 5aab43f) in a third-party harness that is itself marked WIP and has been dormant since 2023-12-14.
measurement_notes: Read in tests/roundTrip.cpp: the lossless check averages the error over differing pixels only and compares it with a per-image tolerance. The tolerance is 0.0 for the MR, CT and MG images, so the harness proves bit-exact round trips there. The 8-bit colour US image uses 6.0 because that list includes lossy libjpeg-turbo8, so the harness does not enforce losslessness for OpenJPH or OpenJPEG on that image. Each decode is timed once with std::chrono::high_resolution_clock. OpenJPEG's timed decode also calls opj_get_cstr_info and never frees the result, a small extra cost and a leak. None of this changes the order of magnitude; it backs the existing B tier and gives no reason to retier.
